summary.abstract: A clinical cohort of 2,140 women recruited in pregnancy through antenatal clinics and perinatal mental health services, with repeated mood assessments from the first trimester to two years after the birth and linked birth outcomes.
summary.description: Standardised mood and anxiety questionnaires are repeated at seven time points, with a structured clinical interview at 32 weeks of gestation and six months after the birth. Medicines taken in pregnancy and birth outcomes come from the maternity record.
summary.title: Bridgewater Perinatal Mood Study (BPMS)

origin.collectionSituation: Cohort, study, trial;,;Secondary care - Outpatients;,;Patient report outcome

access.accessService: Applications are reviewed by the study steering group. Mood questionnaire data are released as de-identified files; linked maternity data are analysed in a secure environment.
access.accessRequestCost: Low cost: free for academic use; a contribution to data preparation is asked for commercial projects.

recruitment.samplingMethod: Women with and without a history of mental illness were invited in a 1:2 ratio from perinatal mental health services and routine antenatal clinics.

followUpSchedule.note: Assessments in each trimester, at six weeks, six months, one year and two years after the birth.

eligibility.inclusionCriteria: Pregnant, aged 18 or over, less than 16 weeks of gestation and able to complete questionnaires in English.
eligibility.exclusionCriteria: Current psychosis or substance dependence at recruitment.
